# pr-2071: gh-2070 [ci-red] v1.0.695 failed

## Description

Closes #2070
### Root Cause
`Cube kernel live (macOS)` was killed by its own `timeout-minutes: 10` while its first step — a plain github.com `actions/checkout` — was still stalled (9m32s against a 1–3 s baseline; 8 observed runs have full-job walls of 68–114 s). The job concluded `cancelled`, the platform-leg verdict in `Quality gate` reds on anything not success/skipped (#1368), and the release train died downstream: `Auto-release` skipped, provenance never signed, and `Advance vpinned marker` refused to move the marker by design (`pin_release.sh` fail-closed without signed SHA256SUMS). The stall is the documented fa-m5 contention class (gh-2013: ONE host hosting three runner registrations); the ceiling was the tightest on the box and sized to the healthy wall.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`cube-kernel-live`): `timeout-minutes` 10 → 30 — clears the gh-2070 stall with ~20 min of slack, at the sibling hosted-macos leg class (`build-ios`: 30); a genuinely wedged box still fails loudly, just later. Same structural remedy as gh-1778 (test-core budget, v1.0.621).
- `test/ci_cube_kernel_ceiling_guard_test.dart` (new): YAML-level guard pinning AC1 job ceiling ≥ 30, AC2 the leg stays on the `macos-m5` pool, AC3 no step-level `timeout-minutes` under the ceiling reintroduces the kill.

### Test Coverage
- `test/ci_cube_kernel_ceiling_guard_test.dart` — verified RED pre-fix (AC1: expected ≥ 30, actual 10), GREEN post-fix: 3/3 passed.
- Workflow-shape suites against the edited `ci.yml`: `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart`, `release_hygiene_test.dart`, `release_flow_race_test.dart`, `ci_core_shard_timeout_guard_test.dart`, `ci_macos_keychain_serialization_guard_test.dart` + 12 more `ci.yml`-parsing guard files — 246 tests passed, 0 failures.

### Notes
- No product-code change; the cube/keychain tests themselves were green in every observed run. The pub.dev publish was unaffected (dart_ok stays true on platform-only red) — v1.0.695 is published; only the release train and the `vpinned` marker advance were lost to this red.
- Adjacent gaps observed but deliberately not fixed here (documented in `outputs/rca.md`): the degraded-runner watchdog is `pull_request`-only (tag runs have no retrigger) and its detector scans only `failure` jobs — a `timeout-minutes` kill concludes `cancelled` and is invisible to it; the mirror-checkout hardening used by the other self-hosted legs was not ported to this leg (needs new tag/PR-merge-ref handling — larger surface than this ticket warrants).

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository

2. Relax the assert to flag only step caps **not** paired with `continue-on-error: true` (the only shape that converts a slow-but-completing step into a red leg under the ceiling).
